headline_marked: TrueFoundry's [[open-source AI agent harness TrueForge]] cuts task costs by up to 75%
headline: TrueFoundry's open-source AI agent harness TrueForge cuts task costs by up to 75%
summary: TrueForge, released under the MIT License, offers significant cost reductions for enterprise AI agent tasks, potentially saving up to 75% compared to commercial alternatives like Claude Managed Agents.
details: TrueFoundry, a B2B machine learning startup, has released TrueForge, an open-source AI agent harness under the MIT License on GitHub. This tool aims to give developers greater control over AI agents and tools while significantly reducing operational costs.

The company claims TrueForge can cut task completion costs by up to 75% when paired with an open-source LLM like GLM-5.2, compared to Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents with Claude Opus 4.8. Even using the same Opus 4.8 model, TrueForge still offers a 30% saving.

TrueForge is designed to be vendor-neutral, allowing enterprises to use it with their preferred AI models and integrate it into commercial products. It handles the core agent loop, enabling models to reason, call tools, and complete tasks efficiently.

The harness achieves its efficiency through context engineering, which optimizes how much information is sent to the model at each step. This includes delaying tool schema loading, delegating tasks to subagents, and compacting long conversations.

TrueForge also treats the sandbox differently, provisioning it only when an agent needs to execute code or work with files. This reduces unnecessary compute, allowing servers to run more agents concurrently and directly lowering model spending.

While TrueForge is free and open-source, TrueFoundry also offers a paid "AI Gateway" for central control over model access, credentials, and budgets. The company envisions TrueForge working alongside its gateway, channeling traffic through it.

headline_marked: [[Stripe acquires OpenRouter for $7.5 billion]], a massive jump from its $1.3B valuation
headline: Stripe acquires OpenRouter for $7.5 billion, a massive jump from its $1.3B valuation
summary: Payments giant Stripe has confirmed its acquisition of AI model router OpenRouter for an estimated $7.5 billion, a significant increase from its $1.3 billion valuation just three months prior.
details: Stripe officially confirmed its acquisition of OpenRouter, an AI model routing startup. Sources indicate the deal is valued at $7.5 billion, a substantial increase from OpenRouter's $1.3 billion valuation in May.

The acquisition sees OpenRouter's founders reportedly receiving $1.5 billion, exceeding the startup's entire valuation from three months ago. Investors are set to receive the remaining $6 billion from the sale.

The payments giant's interest in an AI model router initially raised questions. A leaked letter from Stripe's founders humorously referenced "the singularity" as a reason, a tongue-in-cheek nod to the transformative impact of AI.

More practically, Stripe sees AI driving an economic uptick, with more companies launching and using its services. OpenRouter's utility for developers aligns with Stripe's position as a large developer platform, offering internal benefits and future agentic offerings.
OpenRouter has stated it will continue to operate independently post-acquisition, with its product, mission, and current commitments remaining unchanged. The deal is expected to close in a few weeks.

This acquisition marks a strategic shift for Stripe, moving beyond its traditional focus on incoming cash management. It positions the company to enter the realm of expense management, particularly for AI-related costs.

By acquiring a leading AI gateway for developers, Stripe gains crucial insight into how coders utilize AI. This move also grants Stripe a degree of influence over AI suppliers, including frontier labs and hyperscalers.
